from datetime import date, datetime, timezone

def test_since_includes_boundary_day_and_skips_earlier(tmp_path):
    readings = [
        make_reading(timestamp=datetime(2026, 3, 9, 23, 59, 59, tzinfo=timezone.utc)),
        make_reading(timestamp=datetime(2026, 3, 10, 0, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)),
        make_reading(timestamp=datetime(2026, 3, 11, 12, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)),
    ]
    out = io.StringIO()
    export_csv(readings, out, since=date(2026, 3, 10))
    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out.getvalue())))
    data = rows[1:]  # skip header, as existing tests do
    assert [r[0] for r in data] == ["2026-03-10T00:00:00+00:00", "2026-03-11T12:00:00+00:00"]

def test_since_default_writes_everything(tmp_path):
    readings = [
        make_reading(timestamp=datetime(2020, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)),
        make_reading(timestamp=datetime(2026, 3, 10, tzinfo=timezone.utc)),
    ]
    out = io.StringIO()
    export_csv(readings, out)
    assert len(list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out.getvalue())))) - 1 == 2
